Some studies suggest that high temperature and high relative humidity can reduce the transmission of COVID-19, with one study finding that "high temperature and high relative humidity significantly reduce the transmission of COVID-19, respectively, even after controlling for population density and GDP per capita of cities" [3]. However, other research has found that the relationship between temperature, humidity, and COVID-19 transmission is more complex, and that these factors alone may not be sufficient to prevent the spread of the virus [1]. In fact, a study published in the European Respiratory Journal found that "the spread ability of COVID-19 would not change with increasing temperature" [1]. Additionally, the World Health Organization has emphasized that relying on climate conditions to manage COVID-19 is misguided, and that proven public health measures such as vaccination, wearing masks, and maintaining physical distance are more effective in controlling the spread of the virus [9]. It is also worth noting that some studies have found that COVID-19 can spread in warm and humid environments, such as swimming pools and saunas, and that the virus can be transmitted in areas with hot and humid climates [0, 2]. Therefore, it is not accurate to say that high temperatures and humidity can prevent COVID-19, and it is essential to follow proven public health guidelines to reduce the risk of transmission [9].
